rows.reason: Script bounds the reading to 'line 31 to the end of line 32' then says 'Find the words no other help at hand', but 'help at hand to summon' is on line 33, outside the range it sets; 'tucked into a dash' is also an unexplained device a child cannot act on.

Lines 74, 76, 86 and 87 checked verbatim ('Whose house is it?', 'Do you know Mr. Rochester?', 'I am the governess.', 'if I had not forgotten'); forgetting-implies-knowing step reaches the key correctly.
'suddenly' is on line 8; clouds, stillness, silent rooks and rain follow in lines 8-11; walks to the key from the evidence.

Supports only the first half of the key (wants the mark gone, lines 26-27); never shows the half that separates it from the distractors, that she asks nothing about whose blood it is. 'That is a housekeeping answer' is a label the child must decode, not evidence, and 'how horrid' is left unaddressed against the 'frightened' option.
'cannot be removed' are the last three words of line 33; lines 37-38 give 'In a few moments no trace of the blood-stain could be seen'; contrast reaches the key.
'Charge it to her like breakages' is on line 48 and Mrs Umney 'came to' on line 49; comparison reading is correct and rules out the literal-breakage option.
Lines 14-15 give 'What do I care about Lucy? She's only a girl,—she can't play at bandy'; dismissal then reason, correctly read as a games test applied to a person.

Never connects the weighing of two wants to the act the question asks about ('So she shut her eyes quite close', line 35), and 'Line 34 says which of the two won' misplaces the deciding words, which are 'cared less' on line 33; the 'pure sacrifice' option ('did not extend so far', line 33) is left unaddressed.
'acted very fairly' is on line 48 and the sentence it starts there runs to 'made up to him for it' on line 49; correctly separates the reason from the eating.
Yap's feelings and 'accepted Tom's attention' on lines 61-62, 'sat still on her bough' on lines 65-66, tears for 'the next ten minutes' on lines 71-72 all check; contrast reaches the key.
'I would not have shown myself' is on line 11 (running to 'for all the world' on 12); the lives of the honest men 'depended upon me alone' on lines 13-14, introduced by 'for' on line 13.
'some here, some there' is on line 22; 'this squire and doctor shall find the stuff' on line 47 within 45-47; contrast of the two speeches is correct.
'meaning of their terms' on line 32, 'a common pirate' on line 33, 'the last one left aboard' on line 35; points to the evidence and handles the honest-hand option.
Silver's 'get me an apple' on lines 50-51, Jim 'into the apple barrel' on line 6, 'the terror I was in' on line 52; the link reaches the key.
Dick begins to rise (line 53), 'someone seemingly stopped him, and the voice of Hands' (line 54), 'a go of the rum' (line 55); correct.
'bits of toys, marbles, and trash' on line 5, 'half an hour of pure freedom' on line 6, middle of the afternoon on line 60, 'rolling in wealth' on line 61; the contrast is true.
'What do you call work?' on line 26 and 'maybe it is, and maybe it ain't' on line 29; shows how the question plants the doubt.
Ben's doubt on line 30 and Tom's 'Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?' on lines 32-33; rare-treat reasoning is correct.
'Ben stopped nibbling his apple' on line 34, 'more and more absorbed' on lines 36-37, asks for a turn on line 38; correct.

Stirred hair and eyes 'wide open... perfectly motionless' on lines 14-15, 'That, and its livid colour, made it horrible' on lines 15-16; reaches the key.

'a disused bell' on line 55 and 'some purpose now forgotten' on line 56; reasoning reaches the key.
'eager face' line 6, comrade worth a risk line 9, 'Even Baskerville fell silent' line 45, overcoat pulled closer line 46; before/after contrast is correct.
